subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should OpenClaw extend Feishu from sender/topic session isolation plus DM dynamic agents into a default-off group per-sender subagent lifecycle with isolated skills, config, and memory?
rationale: The issue asks for new channel behavior that changes identity, memory, permissions, routing, lifecycle, and operator controls; source inspection shows current main only has the lower-level session and DM-agent pieces, so automation cannot choose the permanent product/security boundary.

options.title: Design default-off Feishu group subagents
options.body: Create a Feishu-plugin-owned design for sender/topic routing, private/shared memory namespaces, admin policy, lifecycle cleanup, and quota/cost accounting before implementation.

options.title: Keep existing session and thread paths
options.body: Treat group sender/topic sessions plus explicit thread-bound subagents as the supported behavior and close or narrow this feature request to docs and setup guidance.

options.title: Prototype externally first
options.body: Ask for a plugin or ClawHub proof-of-concept to prove the missing SDK seams before adding OpenClaw core or bundled Feishu contracts.

recommendation.title: Design default-off Feishu group subagents
recommendation.body: Create a Feishu-plugin-owned design for sender/topic routing, private/shared memory namespaces, admin policy, lifecycle cleanup, and quota/cost accounting before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The Feishu package lists @m1heng as the strongest explicit owner signal, and this decision is primarily about Feishu plugin behavior and safety boundaries.
